title: Spain Pitches Incentives, Crews and a 500 Million-Strong Spanish-Speaking Market to India at WAVES Film Bazaar
description: Spain, the Country of Honor at this year’s International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in
body:
Spain, the Country of Honor at this year’s International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, laying out its incentives, locations and crews and pushing for closer co-production ties.

	The panel, “Spain: Where Stories Find Their Stage – Incentives, Locations & Co-production Opportunities,” was part of the Knowledge Series at the 20th edition of the market, which runs Nov. 20-24 alongside the 57th IFFI. Variety Asia editor Naman Ramachandran moderated.
	

	“For us, co-production is a key instrument,” said Camilo Vázquez, deputy director of the Institute of Cinematography and Audiovisual Arts (ICAA), the film agency of Spain’s Ministry of Culture. He pointed to better financing, exchanges between technical and artistic teams, and stories that could connect with audiences in both countries, and described the timing as particularly favorable for India-Spain partnerships.

	For Indian producers weighing Spain as a filming destination, the offer extends beyond its locations. Usha Jadhav, a National Award-winning actor and producer with Spanish company ACortes Films, highlighted the country’s track record with international productions, its range of landscapes and architecture, and skilled crews used to working on both big-budget and independent films. She also cited eight-hour shifts and quieter shooting environments as practical advantages, particularly for sync-sound productions.

	Jadhav said the relationship should not be limited to service work, and made a case for collaborations that bring creative teams together across borders.
	

	“Language is not a barrier, because cinema itself is a universal language,” Jadhav said. “We need human stories.”

	Lara Molina, general coordinator of the Spain Film Commission, outlined the tax incentives available to international productions. Miguel Fabián Salazar, Spain’s economic and commercial counselor in Mumbai for the country’s trade and investment agency ICEX, set out what each side brings. India offers production scale, a large consumer market, a global diaspora and strengths in VFX and animation. Spain offers experienced crews, creative talent and access to Europe and Latin America. Partnerships could run from co-production and financing to distribution, post-production and production services.

	“These points somehow fit together. They are not exclusive. They all feed into each other,” Salazar said, noting that Spanish films and productions were traveling farther internationally while Indian productions and streaming services were growing fast.

	ICEX’s Mumbai office works with producers and distributors on market access, local partnerships, setting up businesses and regulatory requirements. It has also organized business missions involving Indian companies in animation, post-production and gaming.

	For Indian producers looking to develop a project with Spanish partners, Guillermo Rodríguez, director of the Valladolid-based cultural institution Casa de la India, said: “The real roadmap is about building connections and building trust.”

	India and Spain signed their audiovisual co-production agreement in 2012. Rodríguez said the scheme was being updated and that clear guidelines would be issued.

	“If you plan to shoot in both countries or one of the countries, you have to make sure you follow those guidelines precisely. Under the co-production agreement, an Indian producer has to approach NFDC… and the Spanish co-producer has to go to ICAA,” he said.

	NFDC is India’s National Film Development Corporation.

	The session closed with a showcase of five Spanish projects seeking Indian collaborators. These included “My Parents Grand Bazaar,” the feature debut of Andalusian filmmaker Rakesh Narwani; “Serendipia,” an India-Mexico-Spain romance; “The Dragon Letter,” from Ladakh-born director Stanzin Jigmet, based on his short of the same name, which won gold in the narrative category at the 2026 Student Academy Awards; animated project “Mumu”; and documentary “Aana and Aai – The War to Become an Artist.”
	

	Rodríguez noted that the two countries had largely stuck to familiar markets, with Spain looking toward Europe and Latin America and India toward English-speaking territories.

	“Imagine the global Indian industry working with the Spanish-speaking world,” he said. “Because Spain is not just Spain. It’s access to the entire Spanish-speaking world – over 500 million people. So if you can bring those two cultural superpowers together, imagine the potential.”

schema.headline: Spain Pitches Incentives, Crews and a 500 Million-Strong Spanish-Speaking Market to India at WAVES Film Bazaar

title: Korea Box Office: Mystery Thriller ‘White Blast’ Opens at No. 1, Ending Five-Week ‘Chiikawa’ Reign
description: Showbox’s mystery thriller “White Blast” debuted atop the South Korean box office over the weekend of Nov. 20–22, ending the five-week chart-toppin
body:
Showbox’s mystery thriller “White Blast” debuted atop the South Korean box office over the weekend of Nov. 20–22, ending the five-week chart-topping run of Japanese anime sensation “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island.” 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the newly opened local release generated $2.3 million from 310,890 admissions across 1,244 screens, claiming a commanding 39.6% of the weekend market.
	

	Co-directed by Hong Eui-jeong (“Voice of Silence”) and Park Sun-woo and adapted from a stage play, the snowbound thriller stars Kim Yoon-seok as a retiring station master at a remote rural railway station and Koo Kyo-hwan as his newly arrived successor. When a heavy snowstorm isolates the station just as news breaks of an overturned prison bus, the two men discover a corpse inside a railway tunnel and grow increasingly suspicious of one another. Since launching mid-week on Nov. 18, the film has accumulated $3.1 million from 423,196 total admissions.

	Toho’s animated hit “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” moved to second place in its eighth weekend of release, earning $695,853 from 91,328 admissions across 746 screens for 11.5% of receipts. Directed by Kei Oikawa and adapted from the manga by Nagano, the fantasy adventure crossed the three-million-ticket milestone over the frame, pushing its cumulative gross to $23.8 million from 3,069,422 viewers since its Sep. 30 bow.

	Lionsgate’s dystopian prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted in third place, pulling in $471,769 from 59,014 admissions across 832 screens to capture 7.8% of the market. Following its Nov. 18 premiere in South Korea, the franchise installment has grossed $716,430 from 91,632 admissions.
	

	Survival thriller sequel “Fall 2: Deadpoint” placed fourth in its sophomore frame, taking in $405,611 from 53,300 admissions across 744 screens for 6.7% of theatrical revenue. The film has accumulated $1.8 million from 240,826 admissions since its Nov. 11 release.

	Trot superstar Lim Young-woong’s concert film “Lim Young WoongㅣIm Hero The Stadium 2” debuted in fifth place on the admissions chart with 31,535 tickets across just 154 screens, though it generated the weekend’s second-highest revenue total at $676,840 (11.2% market share). Released via CGV on Nov. 18 to celebrate the singer’s 10th anniversary, the live concert documentary has amassed $1.2 million from 61,861 total admissions.

	Damien Chazelle’s 2016 musical romance “La La Land” held sixth place in the second weekend of its theatrical re-release, earning $182,612 from 21,418 admissions across 411 screens for a 3% share. The re-issue lifted the film’s cumulative South Korean haul to $24.6 million from 3,903,309 total viewers.

	Next Entertainment World’s corporate thriller “Final Interview” placed seventh in its third weekend, collecting $134,565 from 18,197 admissions across 508 screens. Directed by Kim Jung-hoon and starring Cho Yi-hyun, Kim Jae-won, Shin Seung-ho, and Kwak Dong-yeon, the release pushed its cume to $2.4 million from 325,273 admissions since its Nov. 4 rollout.

	Local animated adventure “Maca and Roni The Movie: The Great Memory Exploration Adventure!” took eighth place in admissions with $103,757 from 14,307 viewers across 199 screens, lifting its cumulative gross to $289,844 from 41,101 admissions.

	Toho’s anime “Detective Conan: The Counterfeit Case of Ultra 30” placed ninth in admissions with 14,141 tickets across 212 screens, while edging ahead in revenue with $108,272 (1.7% market share) to bring its cumulative run to $1.5 million from 199,460 admissions.

	Rounding out the top 10, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s family comedy “The Cat in the Hat” brought in $59,263 from 8,938 admissions across 255 screens, pushing its localizd total to $451,759 from 66,730 viewers.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $6 million, up from last week’s $4.8 million.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: Mystery Thriller ‘White Blast’ Opens at No. 1, Ending Five-Week ‘Chiikawa’ Reign

title: Ateez Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard 200 for the Third Time This Year; U2’s ‘Carnaval de Luz’ Bows at No. 4
description: The K-pop group Ateez continued its string of chart successes with the No. 1 bow on the Billboard 200 album chart of “Golden Hour: Part 6.” It’s th
body:
The K-pop group Ateez continued its string of chart successes with the No. 1 bow on the Billboard 200 album chart of “Golden Hour: Part 6.” It’s the third time in 2026 that the group has had an EP debut in the top spot; the last such occasion came in July, when they premiered at No. 1 with (you guessed it) “Golden Hour: Part 5,” and they did it with “Part 4” before that in February.

	U2 had the second-biggest premiere of the week, with the band’s first full album of original material in nine years, “Carnaval de Lux,” bowing at No. 4.
	

	The previous Ateez EP debuted with 228,000 equivalent album units, and this new “Part 6” followup didn’t follow terribly far behind, with 195,000 units. Billboard reported that the tally was almost entirely sales-driven, with individual copies that were sold amounting to 191,000 of the 195,000 total. A big factor in the massive physical sales, as is typical for K-pop, was the availability of substantial variants designed to encourage multiple sales among fans, with different collectible items in each package — 32 such vinyl or CD variations altogether, Billboard said.

	With this latest chart-topper, Ateez became the first group to have 10 albums or EPs in the top 10 in the 2020s. Only two very prolific solo artists have managed more this decade: YoungBoy Never Broke Again with 15 and Taylor Swift with 14.

	U2’s bow, like Ateez’s, was also far more dependent on sales than streaming, although there were likely not as many of their fans buying every version they could.. “Carnaval de Luz” debuted with 49,000 equivalent album units; full album sales accounted for 42,500 of those units. There were 18 different physical variants for the U2 album, per Billboard.
	

	Among the eight holdovers in the top 10, Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” was tops, falling one rung to No. 2. With 62,000 units for the week, the blockbuster album was down by only 1%.

	Rounding out the top 10 were Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 3; Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide” and “Stick Season” at Nos. 5 and 7, respectively; Ella Langley’s CMA-winning “Dandelion” at No. 6; SZA’s “SOS” at No. 8; Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” at No. 9; and Lil Baby’s “Fresh,” dropping eight spots to No. 10 in its second week.

schema.headline: Ateez Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard 200 for the Third Time This Year; U2’s ‘Carnaval de Luz’ Bows at No. 4

title: China Box Office: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Opens at No. 1 in Quiet Frame
description: Lionsgate Films’ dystopian prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted atop the mainland China box office during the Nov. 20–22 week
body:
Lionsgate Films’ dystopian prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted atop the mainland China box office during the Nov. 20–22 weekend, collecting RMB39.3 million ($5.9 million) over its three-day opening frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. 

	New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “Traces of Justice” moved to second place after a two-week rebound at the top, grossing $2.1 million in its eighth weekend. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Zhang Ji and Yan Zijie, the multi-decade investigation epic has amassed $113.6 million since its Oct. 1 premiere. Starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li, and Chen Minghao alongside guest appearances by Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu, the drama tracks an elite public security detective solving major criminal cases based on real events.
	

	Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “Resident Evil” placed third, taking in $1.7 million in its seventh weekend to lift its cumulative gross to $83 million since rolling out on Oct. 5. 

	Zhijiang Film Media’s suspense thriller “Love Test” debuted in fourth position, pulling in $1.1 million across its two-day opening frame following a Nov. 21 release. Directed by Hou Xiaoyao from a script co-written with Xu Xiaohu and executive produced by Lu Yang and Wang Hongwei, the Chinese remake of the 2011 Colombian-Spanish thriller “The Hidden Face” stars Feng Shaofeng, Chen Yusi, and Li Meng. The narrative follows a concert pianist whose girlfriend stages her own disappearance to test his fidelity, only for his new love interest to move into his mountain villa and uncover unsettling clues behind the vanishing.
	

	Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ domestic body-swap comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” rounded out the top five, adding $900,000 in its eighth weekend to push its cumulative haul to $65.5 million since opening on Oct. 1. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical feature stars real-life comedic pair Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang as an uninspired middle-aged couple forced to navigate marriage and domestic friction after swapping bodies.

	Mainland China’s overall weekend box office reached $16 million, remaining locked in a sluggish late-fall stretch. Year-to-date box office revenue stands at $4.8 billion, trailing the same period in 2025 by 29.9%.

schema.headline: China Box Office: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Opens at No. 1 in Quiet Frame

title: ‘Glee’ Star Chris Colfer Says He Forgot Kurt Hummel ‘Meant So Much to People’ Because of the ‘Homophobia and Hatred’ He Experienced During the Show
description: Chris Colfer is opening up about what it meant to play his now-beloved “Glee” character, Kurt Hummel, a month after reuniting on stage with his on-
body:
Chris Colfer is opening up about what it meant to play his now-beloved “Glee” character, Kurt Hummel, a month after reuniting on stage with his on-screen love interest and co-star, Darren Criss. 

	Criss (who played Blaine Anderson on the hit show) and Colfer surprised audiences by performing “Baby It’s Cold Outside,” an homage to their “Glee” characters, during the “American Crime Story” actor’s London concert on Oct. 18.
	

	Speaking with People about the evening, Colfer said it “was a really special night for me.” “We had been planning it for months. I was not expecting the reaction that we got,” he said. “I was expecting a few hoots and hollers, maybe a couple of gasps, but I was never expecting to get a standing ovation at Royal Albert Hall.”

	Colfer added that the reception was “really healing, honestly.”  He continued: “Because of the homophobia and hatred that I was exposed to at such a young age during the show, and because of the hatred that the show has received since it stopped airing, I had kind of forgotten that that character meant so much to people. So it was a really, really nice reminder, and I think it was a life highlight for me.”

	Colfer has long been outspoken about the bullying he endured while on the show, and in 2024, even revealed he was warned not to come out as gay. “When I started filming the show, I had a lot of people tell me, ‘Do not come out whatever you do because it will ruin your career.’ So I hid for a little bit,” he said during an appearance on “The View.” “But I also told them, ‘I can’t hide it with my voice… I’m more effeminate than most people. I can’t hide it.’ And they said, ‘Don’t worry. As long as you never address it, you’ll be rewarded for it in the end.’”
	

	Just days after Colfer and Criss’ performance, news broke that Disney+ and Hulu had greenlit a reboot of Ryan Murphy’s musical dramedy series. While Variety reported that original cast member Lea Michele is set to return as Rachel Berry, Colfer has been more ambiguous about his involvement, though he did recently confirm on The Daily Beast’s “Obsessed: The Podcast” that he is having conversations about reprising his role. “From what I heard, it sounded very funny, and it sounded like a good idea. So we’ll see,” he said.

schema.headline: ‘Glee’ Star Chris Colfer Says He Forgot Kurt Hummel ‘Meant So Much to People’ Because of the ‘Homophobia and Hatred’ He Experienced During the Show

title: Don Toliver’s Manchester Concert Evacuated After Suspected Tear Gas Released Into Crowd
description:
Don Toliver’s concert at Co-op Live in Manchester, England ended in an evacuation as tear gas was released in the crowd on Sunday. 

	“It is unders
body:
Don Toliver’s concert at Co-op Live in Manchester, England ended in an evacuation as tear gas was released in the crowd on Sunday. 

	“It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert,” wrote the Greater Manchester Police in a statement. According to police, the evacuation was a precaution, and no “serious injuries” were reported.


	The statement concluded: “Please stay away from the arena whilst emergency services help those that have been at the concert safely make their way to their transport home. A major incident has been declared to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.”
	

	A rep for the force said further updates would be available in the coming hours. Reps for Toliver did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

	In a video shared to X, an official at the concert announced that the show would be finished for the evening “due to unforeseen circumstances.”

	“In your own time, please make your way to the nearest exit,” he said. “If you require medical assistance, please speak to a member of staff or visit the level zero concourse.”

	On Tuesday, days before the concert, Toliver announced “Nitrous,” his sixth album, would be released Dec. 4. The day prior, Toliver received five nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards, including best new artist, best rap album, best rap performance, best rap song and best melodic rap performance.

schema.headline: Don Toliver’s Manchester Concert Evacuated After Suspected Tear Gas Released Into Crowd

title: Why Another ‘Hunger Games’ Movie Isn’t Coming Anytime Soon
description:
“The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again.

	“Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchis
body:
“The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again.

	“Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchise, has defied expectations and opened to $120 million at the box office, nearly tripling the $44 million opening of the 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.”

	Surely part of the success here is the Jennifer Lawrence factor: The star’s return (alongside Josh Hutcherson) was first reported by Variety nearly a year ago — and the duo’s reunion with fellow franchise veterans Woody Harrelson, Elizabeth Banks and Jena Malone at the film’s New York premiere ignited seismic levels of buzz online.
	

	According to social media analytics firm RelishMix, ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ amassed a social media reach of 652 million. That doesn’t trail far behind the 680 million pre-opening reach of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” — and represents a staggering 66% jump from “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes’” 393 million (more on par with the pre-opening reach of Disney’s “Hexed” at 391.9 million).

	So, in today’s IP-fueled Hollywood landscape, the blazing success of “Sunrise on the Reaping” would light a fire under the asses of most studio execs to get a seventh “Hunger Games” movie on the calendar as swiftly as possible. While it’d be a fool’s bet to call this the definitive end of the franchise on the big screen, the odds of Lionsgate gifting fans another movie announcement this holiday season aren’t exactly in our favor.

	The key here is Suzanne Collins, who has maintained an active creative role in the franchise since the film rights to her planned trilogy were acquired for $200,000 in 2009. Collins co-wrote the screenplay for the first film and has remained deeply involved in each film, working closely with franchise director Francis Lawrence on everything from story development to reviewing final cuts.
	

	After the Jennifer Lawrence-led saga concluded in 2015 with “Mockingjay — Part 2,” the franchise sat dormant until 2020 when Collins published “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The prequel, set 64 years before Katniss Everdeen entered the arena, explores how an 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow became the tyrannical president of Panem. Lionsgate adapted the novel into a 2023 film and remained in lockstep with Collins, announcing its adaptation of “Sunrise on the Reaping” on June 6, 2024: the same day Scholastic unveiled her latest novel.

	At the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, when the topic of a seventh “Hunger Games” movie came up, everyone from the franchise’s creative forces to Lionsgate’s top brass delivered the same message: We’re waiting on Suzanne.


	“She does not do anything in a frivolous fashion,” Lionsgate chairman Adam Fogelson told Variety at the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere. “When she believes she has an important story to tell, I believe she will write it and we will be the beneficiaries of it. But nothing I can say or do — nothing anyone could say or do — is going to shake her core fundamental desire to be inspired to write a great story.”Collins attended the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, joining a behemoth group photo that brought together Lawrence and the vets who worked on the original four films, Rachel Zegler and the “Songbirds and Snakes” crew and the fresh crop of tributes from the latest installment.



	

									Getty Images
	



	The press-shy author didn’t give any interviews, but while signing autographs for fans, she offered an ambiguous two words when asked whether another novel was on the way: “We’ll see.” (Fans on X were considerably less restrained, with one parody account declaring: “SUZANNE COLLINS CONFIRMED A NEW HUNGER GAMES BOOK”).

	Perhaps the fans are right, and this is all one big game of Werewulf, but Lawrence insists that he hasn’t caught so much as a whiff of another book.

	“I’m telling you — the studio doesn’t believe us, I don’t think anybody believes us — but she does not tell us a word,” Lawrence explained. “She gives us no hints if she’s writing or not.” The director added that he doesn’t think the studio is necessarily “comfortable” with the prolonged waits between Collins’ novels: “I think they wish that she’d just be pumping them out. But, you know, she does her thing. And that’s part of what makes them so great.”

	Whichever direction the franchise heads next, the numbers suggest there are limits to its appeal — and that not every trip to Panem is guaranteed to draw the same crowd. 
	

	Haymitch Abernathy’s origin story has struck a significantly stronger chord with the fanbase than President Snow’s, both on the page and on screen. “Sunrise on the Reaping” sold more than 1.2 million U.S. copies in its first week, twice the first-week sales of “Songbirds and Snakes” and three times those of “Mockingjay.” By January 2026, worldwide English-language sales had surpassed 4.4 million copies. 

	That success translated to the big screen: “Sunrise on the Reaping” currently holds the highest audience score on Rotten Tomatoes (94%) and Letterboxd rating (4.1/5) in the franchise, even surpassing the beloved “Catching Fire” (89% audience RT score; 4.0/5 Letterboxd).

	Hollywood has also seen the pitfalls of stretching a franchise beyond its source material to capitalize on its commercial success. Most infamously, HBO forged ahead on a final season of “Game of Thrones” as George R.R. Martin struggled to complete his sixth “A Song of Ice and Fire” novel, culminating in a wildly divisive final season that prompted more than a million fans to petition for a remake. Martin later revealed in 2022 that he had been largely “out of the loop” during the show’s final seasons.

	“If you look at our relationship with Stephenie [Meyer] on ‘Twilight,’ Chad [Stahelski] and Keanu [Reeves] on ‘John Wick,’ or our longstanding relationship with the ‘Saw’ creators, this is a studio that has prided itself on making great content, but never underestimated how important it is that the architects of that creation continue to have a voice in the process,” Fogelson said, reaffirming Collins as “the creative architect” of the “Hunger Games” franchise. “We have made sure that she is a true partner with our studio across the board. And I think the movies, the campaigns, and everything we do are better for it.

	“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is playing in theaters now.

schema.headline: Why Another ‘Hunger Games’ Movie Isn’t Coming Anytime Soon

title: Hailee Steinfeld Confirms ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Return as Kate Bishop
description:
Hailee Steinfeld will return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Kate Bishop in the forthcoming “Avengers: Doomsday.”

	Marvel Studios and Disney A
body:
Hailee Steinfeld will return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Kate Bishop in the forthcoming “Avengers: Doomsday.”

	Marvel Studios and Disney Animation announced the news Sunday with an Instagram post featuring Steinfeld. “Hey, so I’m here with my movie ‘Hexed,’ but it looks like they delivered a chair from a different movie,” said the actress before panning to a black director’s chair with her name on it. 


	“Catch Hailee Steinfeld in Disney’s ‘Hexed’ before she returns in ‘Avengers: Doomsday,'” read the caption. 
	

	Steinfeld previously appeared as Bishop in the 2021 Disney+ series “Hawkeye” and in 2023’s “The Marvels.” In “Hawkeye,” the “Sinners” actress shared the screen with Jeremy Renner’s superhero, while she appeared briefly in a post-credits scene alongside Brie Larson, Teyonah Parris, Iman Vellani and more for “The Marvels.”  

	“It’s really a privilege to be able to play a character that could in any way possibly inspire anyone,” Steinfeld previously told Variety about embodying the beloved comic character. “Kate Bishop is a character that I would have loved to have had growing up — somebody who is completely ambitious, driven and disciplined, and takes it upon herself to do whatever it is she has to do to achieve her goals.”

	And while the full list of MCU characters who will appear in “Avengers: Doomsday” may still be a mystery, her former costar Renner has made it clear he didn’t return as Hawkeye. “No, no, no, no. Not in that one,” said Renner when asked if he was returning for “Doomsday” in an Oct. interview. “’Doomsday’ I’m not in, so the Avengers will probably lose, just so you know… they didn’t call me, so it’s their fault. They’re going to lose.”
	

	Prior to Steinfeld’s announcement, Elizabeth Olsen’s Scarlet Witch was most recently revealed to be joining the film via the season finale of “VisionQuest.” A post-credit scene replayed the ending of 2022’s feature film “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” where Wanda Maximoff eradicated the Darkhold from all of the multiverse before (seemingly) being crushed from within a mountain. But this time, the scene continues with Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom appearing, lifting the rubble off Wanda and addressing her, confirming fan speculation that Wanda would return.

	“Avengers: Doomsday” hits theaters on Dec. 18.

schema.headline: Hailee Steinfeld Confirms ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Return as Kate Bishop

title: John Turturro Says ‘I Still Consider Myself a Beginner’ as He Gets Marrakech Film Festival Tribute Award: ‘Every Job Is Like a First Love’
description:
Though his career has spanned over four decades, John Turturro still feels like it’s just the beginning.

	The 69-year-old actor and filmmaker was
body:
Though his career has spanned over four decades, John Turturro still feels like it’s just the beginning.

	The 69-year-old actor and filmmaker was honored with a tribute award at Marrakech Film Festival on Sunday night, where he was greeted with roaring applause as he mimed the iconic bowling moves of his “The Big Lebowski” character Jesus Quintana. He then gave a heartfelt speech about his work philosophy, which he said he got from his mom and dad.
	

	“I am a very fortunate person to make a good living as an actor, sometimes as a writer, a director, doing something that I deeply love. To put all of yourself into what you do and give a piece of that away in your work is something that I learned from my parents,” Turturro said. “They taught me that a job well done defines who you are. Building a house, making a dress was done brick by brick, stitch by stitch.”

	He called filmmaking the “magic and beauty of life” and “an offering that you hope others will receive with open hearts.”

	“A great writer, Cesare Pavese, once said that the only great thing in life is to begin. And I still consider myself a beginner in many ways,” he concluded. “For me, when I do a job, every job is like a first love. And I consider this award an encouragement to continue to try.”

	The award was presented to Turturro before a screening of his latest movie, “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” with director Noah Segan and producer Rian Johnson also on hand. The crime thriller stars Turturro as an aging pickpocket who steals a valuable USB drive from the heir to a crime family and must race to return it before the life of his disabled wife is threatened. Initially premiering at Sundance Film Festival earlier this year to praise from critics, the film was picked up by Sony Pictures Classics and released wide in U.S. theaters on Oct. 30.
	

	“As you get older, your toolbox of experience becomes fuller,” Turturro said of taking on the role. “You may not be able to jump as high or run as fast, but I absolutely think this is one profession that you can improve your product because you can learn to distill experiences … It was a gift to work on this film.”

	Turturro, a longtime champion of independent cinema, is perhaps best known for his collaborations with the Coen Brothers on four movies including “The Big Lebowski” and “Barton Fink,” and with Spike Lee on films including “Do the Right Thing” and “Jungle Fever.” He also starred in the “Transformers” film sereies and as supervillain Carmine Falcone in “The Batman” opposite Robert Pattinson. On the TV side, Turturro won an Emmy Award for his performance in comedy series “Monk” and currently stars in Apple TV’s acclaimed sci-fi thriller show “Severance.” 

	Turturro’s Marrakech Tribute Award follows that of Jeff Goldblum, who received the honor from his “The Grand Budapest Hotel” co-star Tilda Swinton. Other starry guests at the festival, whose jury is being led by Oscar winner Marion Cotillard, include Rian Johnson, Luca Guadagnino, James Gray, Monica Bellucci and more. 

	Marrakech Film Festival runs through Nov. 28.

schema.headline: John Turturro Says ‘I Still Consider Myself a Beginner’ as He Gets Marrakech Film Festival Tribute Award: ‘Every Job Is Like a First Love’

title: Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival Prizes: ‘After Elena,’ Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and ‘La Bola Negra’ Win Big
description: Spain’s Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival, one of Europe’s foremost Latin American cinema platforms, prized two of the region’s cinema greats, aw
body:
Spain’s Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival, one of Europe’s foremost Latin American cinema platforms, prized two of the region’s cinema greats, awarding top prizes to Chilean actor Alfredo Castro and Argentine writer-director Lucía Puenzo on Saturday night.

	“La Bola Negra” also reaped yet another plaudit, its scribe-helmer-producer duo Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi – Los Javis – scoring Best Spanish Direction.


	Huelva’s prizes highlight the festival’s focus under director Manuel H. Martín on crossover films, often mixing genre-bending and social issues to surprising effect. Top winner “After Elena.” from Chile’s Shawn Garry, turns on mourning but is a comedy; Lucía Puenzo’s “Pepita, the Gunslinger” is a gangster movie but the gangster is a woman who battles corruption. “Funk,” which won Duda Santos best actress, is a musical but “revolutionary,” says director Aly Muritiba, in its centering “Black joy.”
	

	The 2026 awards also may be the gayest in Huelva’s history, with nearly half going to LGBT movies in a year where Variety has asked whether the 2026-27 Oscars season is their gayest ever.

	The double nods for the Shawn Garry directed “After Elena”(“Después de Elena”) also underscore what Huelva does best: Highlighting titles that deserve further recognition which in the case of Latin America includes most of its movies, given they are under-covered by the international media.

	A TIFF world premiere sold by Meikincine and lead produced by Gabriela Sandoval out of her Cine Matriz label, “After Elena” is not just a study of grief but also a family dynamics comedy with the children of Roberto, 70, moving into his home to supposedly to look after him but also to get their hands on his wife and their mother Elena’s inheritance.
	

	Sluiced by a playful irony, “After Elena” took home Huelva’s Golden Columbus and Best Actor for Castro, once described by Variety as “reliably superb” though here acting against type, abandoning the “heightened performances I’m used to” for “strict, grounded realism,” he told Variety.

	Lucía Puenzo, the celebrated Argentine auteur (“XXY”) and pioneer of Latin American premium TV (“La Jauría,” “Señorita 89”) scored Best Director for “Pepita, the Gunslinger,” which reflects one of the things she does best: Wrapping gender-agenda issues in engrossing thriller narratives. Here Luisana Lopilato (“In Love and in Hate”) plays the real-life Margarita Di Tullio who rebelled against the deaths of fellow sex workers in 1980s Mar del Plata by founding her own brothel and nightlife business empire.

	“La Bola Negra’s” Best Spanish Direction Award in Huelva’s Acento Cine Español section marks the latest recognition from Los Javis’ native Spain, which scored the San Sebastián Festival Audience Award and has grossed a massive €40.4 million ($44.4 million) through Nov. 22, passing “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to become the highest-grossing movie of any nationality in Spain his year, according to Rentrak Spain

	Allan Deberton’s “Gugu’s World,” Brazil’s crowdpleasing International Feature Oscar entry nabbed Huelva’s Audience Award, adding to other kudos such as a Berlin Generation Plus Crystal Bear and Guadalajara Maguey Best Film Award.

	Spain’s Rubén Ochandiano (“Broken Embraces”) scooped Best Supporting Actor for his performance as a musician who galvanizes the protagonist’s life in Mexican Lorena Villarreal’s “Life Is” (“La Vida Es”).

	Elsewhere, Huelva’s awards spotlighted disparate talents to track. Sharon Kleinberg’s “I Am Mario” walked off with Huelva’s Special Jury Prize. It turns on Mario, a forty-year-old trans taxi driver who faces an unexpected pregnancy which fulfils his dream to become a father but shatters some of his beliefs about masculinity. “I Am Mario” also won at Guadalajara Film Fest’s Maguey section , scooping its Jury Award in April.

	Best Actress was won by Brazil’s Duda Santos the skyrocketing star of telenovelas “Garota do Momento” and “A Nobreza do Amor” who plays in Aly Muritiba’s “Funk” a sassy, sexually frank funk singer MC Sabrina whose on-stage persona hides a fragility exposed during her pursuit of fame.
	

	Santos already shared with MC Nem a Tribeca 2026 Special Jury Mention for Best Performance in an International Feature. Huelva can now claim it was one of the first festivals in the world to recognise and prize Santos.

	Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival 2026 Awards

	Golden Colombus, Best Feature Film: “After Elena,” directed by Shawn Garr

	Special Jury Prize: “I am Mario,” directed by Sharon Kleiberg

	Best Director: Lucía Puenzo for “Pepita, the Gunslinger” (“Pepita, la pistolera”)

	Best Actor: Alfredo Castro, for “After Elena”

	Best Actress: Duda Santos, for “Funk”

	Best Supporting Actor: Rubén Ochandiano, for “Life Is”

	Best Spanish Direction: Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi for “La Bola Negra”

	Silver Columbus Audience Award: “Gugu’s World,” directed by Allan Deberton

	City of Huelva Honorary Award: Paulina García

	Silver Columbus, Best Andalusian Direction: Elías Pérez for “Plus Ultra”

schema.headline: Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival Prizes: ‘After Elena,’ Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and ‘La Bola Negra’ Win Big

title: '90 Day Fiancé' Star Sheila Mangubat Dead at 35
description:
'90 Day Fiancé' Alum
                          Sheila Mangubat Dead at 35
body:
'90 Day Fiancé' Alum
                          Sheila Mangubat Dead at 35
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                November 22, 2026
                
                            5:22 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 22, 2026
                                1:15 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              '90 Day Fiancé' star Sheila Mangubat has died just days before her 36th birthday.
      
    
              Sheila's former fiancé David Dangerfield shared the news on Instagram, writing ... "It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines. I am devastated and still trying to process this loss."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              Sheila's brother Jonathan also shared a video of her funeral Sunday to his Facebook stories ... hours after posting a clip of him and his family mourning her on her deathbed.
      

              Despite breaking up in Oct. 2025 after years of going long-distance and K-1 visa setbacks ... David said he had rekindled his romance with Sheila in June 2026.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              As you know ... David and Sheila connected on a Facebook group for deaf singles.
      
    
              Their romance and engagement were featured on Season 6 of "90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days."
      
    
              Sheila was 35 years old.
      
    
              RIP

title: 'Party of Five' Star Scott Wolf Reveals Dad Steven Is Dead at 82
body:
Scott Wolf's Dad
                          Dead at 82
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Scott Wolf has revealed that his father, Steven Wolf, has died.
      
    
              Taking to Instagram, the former "Party of Five" actor shared that his dad passed away a couple of days ago.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              He wrote ... "His passing leaves a hole in the center of our hearts, and our lives. He was my hero, and I have lived my entire life trying to be like him. He was the most kind, honest, caring, and loving man."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              He added ... "He was brilliant, funny, and truly made every room, and this world, a better place."
      
    
              Steven's death comes 2 months after Scott and his estranged wife, Kelley Wolf, shared that they'd be proceeding with a divorce.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Scott had initially filed for divorce in June 2025, before obtaining a temporary restraining order against Kelley as well as receiving temporary custody of their kids.
      
    
              Kelley has since chalked up her behavior at the time to a drug-induced mania.
      
    
              Steven was 82.
      
    
              RIP

body:
Usher & Chris Brown's Tour
                          Fire Performer Goes Down in Flames
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Usher and Chris Brown's tour has suffered another drama-filled moment after a fire performer was seen falling off the stage.
      
    
      
      yeah it’s time to wrap this tour up. https://t.co/90ZF7PHtve
              @layahsfanta
          
  
    
              In a video captured from the singers' second night of shows in New Orleans ... the performer -- who was twirling around a LOT of fire -- can be seen walking backward before falling down some stairs.
      
    
              As you know ... the tour has not been the smoothest operation.
      
    
              TMZ broke the story ... the two singers had a huge backstage argument earlier this month at one of their shows in Atlanta.
      
    
              We're told their egos got the better of them ... and that the two had got into a heated debate about how to proceed after fans were delayed getting to the stadium due to traffic.
      
    
              Sources told us that the pair's respective teams were trying to work around the clock to get them to sit down and clear the air.
      
    
              We've reached out to Live Nation and Chris and Usher's reps for comment on the fire performer's status ... so far, no word back.

title: Billy Joel Motorcycles Sell for Roughly 5 Times Their Estimate
description:
Billy Joel
                          Motorcycles Sell for 5 Times More Than Estimate
body:
Billy Joel
                          Motorcycles Sell for 5 Times More Than Estimate
                      
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
              Billy Joel is known for smashing the record for most shows performed at Madison Square Garden ... but this weekend, he also pulled off another rare feat -- selling his motorcycles for five times their estimate.
      
    
              Gooding Christie’s auctioned off a total of 69 of his motorcycles and raised more than $2 million -- roughly quintupling their pre-auction estimate of $405,000.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Of course, this was all for a good cause ... with the proceeds benefiting the Joel Foundation.
      

              Each and every lot sold exceptionally well ... often 5 to 10 times their estimated values! Talk about a Big Shot!
      
    
              The standout sale, however, was his 1978 Triumph Bonneville T140 'Madison Square Garden' Custom.
      
    
              Given to BJ as a gift for his 150th sold-out MSG performance, it fetched $577,000 ... more than 50 times the $10K-$15K projected value.
